fields.Name: T057 - AI Configuration
fields.Description: Opens the AI application's Configuration section once, then walks its bespoke UX (inline card expansion, grid/list view toggle with detail panel), verifying each via checkpoints. Consolidates old T127-T128.

InputDefinition.goal: Assume you are already logged in at http://localhost:4200. Open the AI application using the application switcher dropdown next to the logo (NOT the Ctrl+K search box), then open the Configuration section. Then walk these sections IN ORDER, and as you arrive at each set "checkpointReached" to the exact checkpoint name shown: (1) config-card-expansion - in grid view, click a configuration card's header to expand it inline and reveal nested detail (its Configuration Parameters and/or associated Prompts), then click again to collapse it (a valid empty state counts if there are no configurations); (2) config-detail-and-view-toggle - switch the view toggle from Grid to List (and back) to confirm the layout changes between card grid and table, then trigger the open/details action on a configuration to open its detail panel showing status, description, and stats. Keep going until both sections have been visited. Pages can take 10-30s to load in this resource-constrained environment - wait for content rather than navigating away.

checkpoints.name: config-card-expansion
checkpoints.instruction: expand a configuration card inline to reveal nested detail
visualCriteria: Clicking a configuration card header expands it inline to reveal nested content (Configuration Parameters and/or associated Prompts) and it collapses on a second click - OR a valid empty state is shown

checkpoints.name: config-detail-and-view-toggle
checkpoints.instruction: toggle grid/list view and open a configuration detail panel
visualCriteria: The Grid/List view toggle switches the configuration layout between cards and a table, AND triggering the open/details action opens a detail panel with the configuration's status/description/stats - OR a valid empty state is shown
